page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on KVM virtualization and powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores via multithreading, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded compute capability, highlighted by a strong stress-ng single-core score of 3073.57 that places it in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Multi-core compute and data compression tasks fall into the median tier, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 6150.83 and single-threaded gzip compression at 28.95 GB/sec. However, high-concurrency throughput tests reflect resource constraints typical of a 4-vCPU topology: multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (26.39 GB/sec), PassMark database operations (2068.79), static web serving throughput (5.45 GB/sec), and Redis SET throughput (5.7 million ops/sec) score in the lower quartile.

Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.g8a.xlarge provides balanced resource density for non-storage-intensive compute tasks. Because local persistent disks are absent and baseline network bandwidth is capped at 2 Gbps, I/O-intensive workloads rely on external cloud storage services, introducing network latency and throughput tradeoffs. The server is well configured for intermediate application tiers, standard container hosting, CI/CD worker nodes, and general utility microservices, whereas heavy database engines and high-volume web endpoints require larger instance sizes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) on an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM. Operating on KVM, the x86_64 platform features hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instructions. The instance provides 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, it registers strong single-core compute performance alongside average multi-core and compression scores, though database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and web throughput show lower-tier performance due to the 4-vCPU resource limit. It serves standard enterprise applications, microservices, and general compute workloads effectively.
